d: Retrieval triggered during generation, not just at start; model decides when to query based on generated content. HyDE and self-RAG are examples.
Lightweight modules inserted in transformer layers trained on specific tasks; combined with context for efficient multi-task performance.
Dynamically adjusting context composition based on the current task, user query, or observed model behavior mid-conversation
Structured memory holding an agent's beliefs, goals, preferences, and accumulated experience; feeds into context_building for downstream tasks
RAG where the LLM orchestrates multiple retrieval steps, decides what to query, and synthesizes from multiple sources. Reflection and planning loops.
Attention with Linear Biases — a position embedding scheme derived from attention scores, enabling better length extrapolation than absolute positions
The data structure or index built to support approximate_nearest_neighbors queries over a vector collection
Fast retrieval of roughly similar vectors accepting some error; enables scaling vector_database beyond exact search limits
Algorithms that trade exactness for speed in vector_search, enabling sub-linear retrieval over large embedding indices
Recall triggered by related concepts; attention mechanism is a form of content-addressable associative memory enabling retrieval by similarity.
Retrieving memories by content similarity rather than exact match; enabled by embedding space proximity.
Perspective that attention mechanism itself is a form of memory retrieval; queries search keys to retrieve values, analogous to content-addressable memory.
The computational bottleneck created by the O(n²) cost of self_attention as context_length grows; the core challenge in long_context
Computational cost scaling quadratically with sequence length; O(n^2) in naive attention. Flash attention and sparse methods mitigate this.
Stochastic masking of attention weights during training; regularization technique with indirect effects on context_utilization patterns
The core operation allowing each token to attend to all others; scaled dot-product attention is the standard. Memory and context are both outputs of attention computation.
Computational overhead of attention mechanisms relative to other operations; dominates total compute for long contexts.
The specific matrix of attention weights produced by a model for a given context; observable via attention visualization for interpretability
Computational cost of self_attention that scales as the square of context_length; the fundamental reason long context_length is expensive
Condition where attention weights become uniform across long context; signals reduced context_utilization and effective_context shrinkage
Position index in context_length where attention_saturation begins; typically occurs when context_length exceeds a model-dependent threshold
Certain tokens (often BOS/start tokens) disproportionately accumulate attention weight; hypothesis: they serve as a computational anchor for softmax normalization without carrying semantic meaning.
Fixed or learned position indices within context_length that accumulate disproportionate attention mass
Special tokens that accumulate disproportionate attention mass, enabling efficient long-context modeling without explicit positional encoding
The phenomenon where models develop increasingly sparse attention patterns for distant tokens, often losing middle information (lost_in_the_middle)
The distribution of attention weights across tokens; narrow spread means concentrated computation on few tokens, wide spread means distributed computation.
Inspecting attention_pattern matrices to understand what tokens the model is attending to; used for debugging and interpretability
Distribution of attention scores across context tokens; reveals what the model considers relevant to current generation
Tracing model outputs back to source context tokens or retrieved memories; essential for factual grounding and verification
Retrieval of past context tokens; constrained by context_window for working_memory and retrieval_mechanism for long_term_memory
Maximum token positions behind current index extractable via backward_recall; constrained by context_length and attention_weighting patterns
Model's current representation of world facts and user claims; maintained through context and updated via retrieval
A probabilistic sparse retrieval ranking function; the standard lexical baseline against which dense_retrieval is compared
A subword_tokenization algorithm building vocabulary via frequency-based merges; used by GPT models

Attention entropy: a scalar measure of the uniformity/dispersion in attention_weighting distributions across context tokens; high entropy signals near-uniform attention (low selectivity) while low entropy indicates focused attention on key tokens.

Retrieval accuracy at position: the fraction of relevant facts or context atoms correctly accessed when queried from a given token distance; varies with position_embedding type and context_horizon boundaries.
Task performance variance: measurable change in downstream task accuracy when the same information is repositioned within context_window; reveals position-dependent bias in effective_context.
Attention saturation: condition where attention_weighting becomes uniform across long context, reducing selective focus and shrinking effective_context toward a uniform distribution.

Attention sinks artifact: disproportionate attention mass accumulating on specific tokens (often BOS) that enables stable gradients in long sequences; directly affects how context_utilization degrades with sequence length.
Information decay curve: function mapping token distance from current position to usefulness of that token for generation; describes how backward_recall fidelity degrades across context_horizon.
Useful information density: ratio of tokens causally traced as contributing to output versus total tokens in context_window; the efficiency ratio of memory_efficiency applied to working_memory.
Effective context ratio: effective_context measured as fraction of context_length; if ratio < 1.0 the model fails to leverage all available tokens for the generation task.

Context compression quality: how much redundant or non-contributory context exists per unit of useful signal; measured by causal_tracing where low-contribution tokens indicate poor context compression.

Position sensitivity bias: systematic performance degradation at context_horizon boundaries or with certain position_embedding types (sinusoidal vs RoPE vs ALiBi) that affects retrieval accuracy at position.
Sliding window efficiency: how well sliding_window evicts old tokens while preserving high-attention_sinks and useful context atoms; relates to memory_efficiency in the working_memory layer.
Algorithm for deciding which KV pairs to discard when cache is full; options: LRU, LFU, importance-weighted, or learned policies.
Abrupt loss of previously learned knowledge when training on new data; mitigated by experience_replay and importance_weighted_memory
Technique identifying which context tokens causally influence model outputs; used to understand effective_context and attention patterns
Token position within context_length selected as intervention point during causal_tracing to measure influence on output
Producing intermediate reasoning steps before final answer; when demonstrated in context, subsequent reasoning follows the pattern. A form of contextual procedural memory.
Tokens within context_length reserved for scratchpad reasoning steps; reduces output_capacity by its byte length
The logical seams between chunks; optimal placement preserves semantic coherence and avoids splitting entities or instructions mid-chunk
Embedding a text chunk — a segment of a document — rather than an entire document or a single sentence; balances granularity for retrieval
How documents are split into retrieval units; choices affect recall/precision: fixed-size, semantic (by sentences/paragraphs), recursive, or agentic splitting.
Condition (time passed, memory fullness, importance threshold) that initiates memory_consolidation from episodic to semantic storage
Gradual reduction in retrieval probability for older memories based on forgetting_curve principles
Composing final context from preprocessed components: system prompt, conversation history, retrieved documents, memory entries. Ordered according to template.
Reasoning constrained by available context; unlike humans who can use unbounded external memory, LLM reasoning limited to context window.
The hard edge position within context where context_overflow triggers if exceeded; exactly context_length minus one for the output region.
The process of assembling the prompt from system instructions, conversation history, retrieved documents, and tool outputs into a coherent input sequence
Storing computed key-value pairs from prior forward passes to avoid recomputation on repeated or overlapping context prefixes
Tokens consumed by caching metadata that reduce net available context_length for content
The ratio of tokens actively processed to total available context_length; quantifies context_utilization as used_capacity divided by max_model_tokens.
The absolute hard upper bound on total sequence length enforced by model architecture; once reached context_overflow occurs
A discrete unit of text stored for retrieval; typically 512-1024 tokens. The granularity at which retrieval operates.
Dividing long content into manageable segments (chunks) for separate embedding, retrieval, and context_building
The logical consistency and narrative unity of context content; incoherent context can cause the model to contradict itself
Transforming a large context into a shorter equivalent representation — via summarization, extraction, or lossy summarization — to fit within context_limit
Ratio of original information size to compressed representation; tradeoffs with fidelity: higher compression means more information loss.
The breadth of distinct perspectives, information sources, or viewpoints represented in context; can improve robustness but dilute signal
Selecting which tokens/chunks to remove when context is full; strategies: FIFO, importance-weighted, semantic clustering, or learned eviction.
All available context tokens used with no room for more; requires eviction, summarization, or termination of context-dependent operations.
Growing the effective context beyond a single context_window by chaining windows or using hierarchical summarization
The accuracy with which context content reflects ground truth; low fidelity leads to hallucinated reasoning from corrupted context
Ensuring generation is anchored in the provided context rather than ungrounded model knowledge; key for retrieval_augmented_generation quality
How many historical context states are retained for potential backtracking or recovery; larger windows enable undo but cost memory.
Farthest retrievable or presentable token distance from current position; the effective reach of memory_access
Token span from first to last position that falls within context_horizon; bounded above by context_length
Adding new information to context without rebuilding it from scratch; the standard online mode for multi-turn conversations
Programmatically adding information to context at runtime; used for dynamic retrieval, tool results, or user-provided information.
Ensuring context from one request doesn't leak into another; critical for multi-user systems with shared infrastructure.
Total number of tokens (input + output) an LLM supports; the hard ceiling on how much text can be loaded into context_window at once
Predicting how many tokens a text passage will produce; required for accurate token budgeting before generation.
Techniques (position_interpolation, RoPE scaling) enabling models to handle longer context than trained on
Maximum tokens a model can attend to; beyond this, information is invisible. Models like GPT-4-128k have different limits than Llama-8b's 32k.
The challenge of maintaining model quality and retrieval accuracy as context_length grows; quadratically harder for attention and retrieval
The practical or configured maximum token count enforced during inference, often less than the theoretical context_length due to memory or cost constraints
Strategies and systems for selecting, ordering, compressing, and evicting content to stay within context_window while preserving task relevance
Combining multiple context sources (retrieved, historical, generated) into unified context fed to model; requires conflict resolution and ordering.
The failure state where total input exceeds context_window, causing silent truncation or errors depending on the client library
The policy and mechanism for responding when content exceeds context_limit — whether to truncate, reject, compress, or paginate
Condition where total token count exceeds context_length; activates truncation_strategy
Tokens consumed by system prompts, chat templates, or fixed prefixes that reduce prompt_capacity even when not user-provided
Degree of shared information between retrieved memories and current context; affects redundancy and memory_efficiency
Appending empty tokens to extend context to alignment boundaries; inefficient but sometimes necessary for batch processing
Injecting misleading information into context to manipulate model behavior; can occur via retrieval from adversarial sources or deliberate prompt injection.
How token positions are represented to the model; affects relative distance awareness and context extrapolation ability.
Transforming generated output: formatting, validation, security filtering. Not memory but completes the context lifecycle.
Transforming raw inputs into context-ready format: cleaning, formatting, metadata extraction, chunking. Done before context assembly.
Selective removal of low-relevance tokens, messages, or chunks from context to improve signal-to-noise ratio and reduce token spend
The mathematical reality that self_attention cost grows quadratically with sequence length; fundamental limit on practical context_length
The signal-to-noise ratio, relevance, coherence, and grounding quality of content within context_window; distinct from raw token count
Granularity at which context_length is quantized in a given system; often 1 token but may be larger for efficiency in specific implementations
Overlap or duplication of information within context; reduces effective context length and can bias model toward redundant content.
Periodically rebuilding context from persistent sources rather than incrementally extending it, reducing error accumulation from noisy truncation
The degree to which context content directly pertains to the current query or task; a primary criterion for context_selection
Assessing whether context entries help answer current query; used to filter retrieved content before injection.
Clearing all or part of context to start fresh; may reset working memory while preserving system prompt, or full reset to initial state.
The runtime mechanism or policy invoked when context_length must accommodate inputs exceeding current capacity; involves reallocation or overflow handling.
The multiplier relating raw context_length to effective_context; models with improved attention patterns achieve factors closer to one.
Choosing which items (documents, messages, facts) enter the context based on relevance, recency, or importance heuristics
Capturing the full state of context at a specific point in time for later comparison, auditing, or resumption
Snapshot of all current context tokens and their metadata; includes user messages, system prompts, retrieved documents, memory entries, and generated text.
Replacing a long context segment with a distilled summary that preserves key semantics while consuming fewer tokens
Managing the transition when conversation topic shifts; requires knowing when to discard or archive prior context
Combining information from multiple retrieved sources into coherent context; requires resolution of conflicts, deduplication, and ordering.
Information density per context token; higher efficiency means more useful information fits in limited context. Affected by chunking, retrieval quality, and compression.
Monitoring what information is currently in context; enables informed decisions about eviction, retrieval, and context updates.
Hard-cutting context to max_tokens, typically from the oldest or lowest-scored entries; the simplest form of context_management
How effectively the model uses all available context tokens; metrics include attention entropy, retrieval accuracy at various positions, task performance variation with position.
Ratio of effective_context_limit to token_budget; attention_saturation lowers this rate on long contexts
The finite token sequence an LLM can process in a single forward pass; defines the maximum input + output capacity bounded by architecture or inference config
The absolute position index equal to context_length minus one; tokens cannot be positioned beyond this limit without triggering context_overflow
Active control of what enters, stays in, and leaves the context window; requires eviction policies, prioritization, and summarization.
Adding padding tokens to fill context to fixed length; used for batching but wastes compute on padding tokens.
Fraction of context window actively used for task-relevant information; low utilization means wasted tokens, high utilization maximizes information density.
Adaptive rate at which new information from context is incorporated into model's implicit beliefs; varies by architecture
Reducing conversation history to essential elements; options: keep last N turns, summarize early turns, keep only user intents or key facts.
The chronological log of user_message and assistant_message turns in a session; the primary raw material for context_building
The aggregate of discourse_memory, entity_tracking, and conversation_history that defines the current interaction state
Identifying when multiple expressions refer to the same entity or concept in text; reduces fragmentation in context_building and memory_write
RAG variant where retrieved documents are evaluated for correctness before use; incorrect retrievals trigger re-retrieval or fallback to parametric knowledge.
A similarity measure between embedding vectors based on the cosine of the angle between them; invariant to vector magnitude
Attention mechanism where queries attend to a separate context (e.g., retrieved documents); enables retrieval_augmented_generation
Memory accessible across multiple sessions for a given user or agent, enabling continuity of preferences, facts, and relationship history

Metric quantifying the uniformity (or peakedness) of attention_weighting distribution across context tokens; maximum entropy means uniform attention (poor context_utilization), low entropy means focused attention on relevant tokens.
Statistical measure (e.g., Gini coefficient or KL divergence from uniform) of attention_weighting distribution; directly quantifies soft_attention versus sparse_attention behavior in practice.
The ratio of tokens that causally influence model output (via causal_tracing) to the total context_window capacity; values below 1.0 indicate unused or attention_saturation-blunted context.
Ratio of effective_context tokens to total context_window capacity; quantifies what fraction of available context the model actively leverages
The proportion of context tokens that carry task-relevant information versus padding or redundant content; higher density improves effective_context utilization per token budget.

Metric comparing model performance on identical tasks when relevant information appears at the beginning (recency/primacy) versus middle versus end of context; a component of context_utilization assessment.
Degree to which task performance varies based on token position within context_window; reveals where in the context the model attends most effectively

Task performance metric measuring how accurately the model retrieves or utilizes information located at specific token positions within context_window; reveals positional bias in working_memory access.
Accuracy of backward_recall for context tokens at varying positions from current generation point; measures how precisely the model retrieves relevant information from memory_window
The context_token distance from current position at which attention_saturation onset occurs; determines the practical context_horizon for reliable working_memory retrieval.
Ratio of task-relevant tokens to irrelevant or distracting tokens present in the active context; low ratio degrades cu_information_density

Quantitative measure of task accuracy change as relevant context tokens are relocated to different positions; fundamental context_utilization signal showing how position_embedding quality affects effective_context.
Constraint in memory_hierarchy that limits context_utilization; can be computational (attention_mechanism), positional (position_embedding), or retrieval-based (backward_recall)
Conscious knowledge of facts and events; analogous to explicit semantic_memory and episodic_memory in LLM systems
A continuous-valued vector representation produced by a neural encoder; the standard output of text_embedding models
Retrieval using dense embedding vectors produced by a neural encoder; captures semantic similarity better than sparse methods
Memory system with learnable read/write operations; gradients can flow through memory access, enabling the model to learn what to store.
High-level structure of conversation: goals, commitments, questions raised; persists beyond individual turn context
Retrieving results that cover different aspects of a query rather than near-duplicates; improves coverage but may reduce average relevance.
A similarity measure using raw dot product between embedding vectors; sensitive to magnitude and used when embeddings are normalized
Allocating variable token budgets to different context components (history vs retrieved docs vs system prompt) based on task requirements
Portion of context_window the model actually leverages for any given generation; often less than the full window due to attention patterns
Portion of context_length the model actually leverages for a given task; often less than full token_budget due to attention patterns
The empirically observed maximum usable context before performance degradation; often lower than model_native_limit due to attention_saturation
Attention variants reducing quadratic complexity: linear attention, performer (random feature approximation), cosformer, or state space models.
The surrounding context of an event including user inputs, system responses, and environmental state at the time.
Signal indicating episode boundaries: new session start, task boundary, or conversational turn demarcation.
A discrete unit of experience stored in episodic memory — a single interaction, task completion, or notable outcome.
An ordered collection of events forming a coherent experiential arc; the episodic unit of storage.
Structured log of the exchange pairs (prompt/response) comprising an event.
The result or consequence of an event — success, failure, or partial completion — recorded for outcome-based retrieval.
Algorithm for reducing salience weights of older events over time; models forgetting in episodic memory.
Numeric value indicating how memorable or significant an event is; influences consolidation priority and retrieval ranking.
Ordering structure by event importance or impact; enables retrieval by significance rather than recency.
Captured system state (context window contents, active variables, user profile) at the moment of an event.
Organizational structure mapping events to time ranges; enables retrieval by temporal proximity.
Temporal marker indicating when an event occurred; enables chronological ordering of episodic entries.
Number of dimensions in the embedding_space; higher captures more nuance but increases storage and retrieval_cost
A model trained to produce text_embedding vectors; may be a general encoder like CLIP, a domain-specific encoder, or a late-intercept from an LLM
Connecting text spans to entries in a knowledge base or knowledge_graph, enabling structured memory storage and disambiguation
Determining that two references refer to the same underlying entity; critical for coherent knowledge retrieval and memory merging across sources
Identifying and maintaining references to specific entities across turns; challenged by coreference_resolution complexity
High-capacity short-term store holding recent episodes in near-raw form before consolidation into semantic_memory
Memory storing discrete experiences or events — specific interactions,完成任务, or notable outcomes — organized chronologically or by significance
A geometric distance measure between embedding vectors; used in nearest-neighbor search when angular similarity is insufficient
Retrieving by exact key match rather than similarity; used for metadata lookups, identifiers, or when exact terms are required.
Technique of mixing past examples into training batches; combats catastrophic forgetting in continual learning
Conscious, accessible memory that can be verbalized; in LLM context, retrieved via RAG or provided in prompt.
Models or techniques enabling effective use of context beyond the training context_length; requires architectural innovations or inference tricks
Storage outside the LLM's native parameters — vector databases, graphs, or file systems — that must be retrieved and injected into context
Selecting verbatim or lightly paraphrased spans from source; preserves factual fidelity better than abstractive summarization
Direct retrieval of specific factual assertions from a knowledge store to support or correct LLM generation
Facebook AI Similarity Search: a library of efficient ANN indexes and clustering methods for dense vector retrieval at scale
Degree to which model outputs respect information in provided context; measured by attribution accuracy and hallucination rate
Providing 2-5 examples in context to guide task performance; example selection and ordering affect success significantly.
A memory-efficient attention algorithm using tiling and recomputation to avoid materializing the full n×n attention matrix in HBM
Number of tiles into which flash_attention partitions the context_length squared attention matrix for memory_efficient computation
Loss of information from memory; in vector stores, caused by eviction; in model context, caused by position degradation and attention distribution.
Decay function describing memory retention over time; models this decay in episodic_memory management
Future tokens visible in bidirectional models; limited utility in autoregressive generation but useful in embedding computation
The token allocation remaining for output after input tokens are accounted; varies dynamically per request
Shared memory accessible across all users and sessions; typically contains general facts, policies, or system knowledge.
Physical memory constraints on GPU that limit kv_cache size and thus maximum practical context_length for a given model on given hardware
A database optimized for storing and querying graph-structured data; powers knowledge_graph storage and traversals at scale
Querying a knowledge graph for relevant triples/paths; often combined with vector retrieval in neuro-symbolic RAG pipelines.
Attention focusing on single positions; non-differentiable but efficient; approximated by soft attention in practice
Recursive splitting of text into nested chunks enabling multi-granularity retrieval from summary to detail
A two+ tier context architecture: a short immediate context for recent turns plus a summarized or retrieved outer context for long-range dependencies
Memory organized in levels of abstraction: recent items, summaries of older items, abstract concepts; reduces memory pressure while preserving key information.
Hierarchical Navigable Small World — a graph-based ANN algorithm offering strong recall-speed tradeoffs; implemented in FAISS and most vector DBs
Distributed representation where each memory fragment is encoded across many positions; biologically inspired retrieval mechanism
System combining multiple memory substrates (vector store + knowledge_graph + kv_cache) for complementary strengths
Combining dense_retrieval and sparse_retrieval — often via reciprocal rank fusion — to capture both semantic and lexical matches
Hypotheses-to-Documents: generate hypothetical answer, embed it, retrieve real documents matching the hypothesis; improves recall on ambiguous queries.
Unconscious memory affecting behavior without explicit recall; in LLMs, manifested as in-context behavioral patterns not easily articulated.
Memory entries weighted by estimated importance; higher weight reduces eviction probability. Importance estimated by recency, access frequency, or model-assessed relevance.
Model adapts behavior based on examples provided in the context window; no weight updates. Related to memory since examples must fit in context.
Retrieval from memory systems kept in RAM rather than disk; faster but limited capacity. Often used for hot data with cold storage for scale.
Reducing the memory footprint of an ann_index through quantization or product quantization, trading recall for storage efficiency
Distributing an ANN_index across multiple machines or partitions to scale retrieval beyond single-node memory and compute
Tokens marking significant boundaries in context (topic shifts, new entities, key claims); candidates for memory_anchors
The portion of token_budget allocated to prompt/prompt_tokens; the maximum tokens a user can submit before generation begins
The portion of context_length reserved and available for prompt tokens, retrieved context, and system instructions before generation begins.
When new information overwrites or degrades retrieval of old information; in append-only stores, occurs during reranking/retrieval; in model context, speculative.
A taxonomic relationship linking a kg_instance to its kg_class, establishing membership and enabling inheritance of class-defined properties and constraints.
Multi-pass retrieval where each pass uses results from previous passes to refine query; continues until model decides sufficient information gathered.
Salient tokens or embeddings flagged for priority retention; used by importance_weighted_memory selection
The generic term for caching kv_cache entries; critical for efficient inference with long conversation_history
Memory organized as key-value pairs where keys enable retrieval by content; resembles attention's key-query matching.
A kg_entity type within the kg_ontology; groups instances that share structural or semantic properties
An abstract kg_entity representing a category or idea; can serve as a class in is_a hierarchies
A node in the knowledge_graph representing a distinct thing — concrete object, person, event, or concept — identified by a unique identifier
Deriving new kg_triple entries from existing ones through rule application or traversal over the kg_ontology (e.g., transitivity of is_a)
A kg_entity that is a specific concrete occurrence of a kg_class; participates in is_a relationships with its class
The schema layer of a knowledge_graph defining allowed kg_entity types (classes), allowed kg_predicate labels, and domain/range constraints on kg_relationships
The label or type of a kg_relationship; defines the semantics of how two kg_entities relate (e.g., is_a, part_of, owned_by, caused_by)
An attribute attached to a kg_entity describing a feature or quality; differs from kg_relationship in that it terminates in a literal value rather than another entity
A typed directed edge connecting a source kg_entity to a target kg_entity; the edge carries a predicate label defining the relation semantics
The structural blueprint specifying which kg_predicate labels are permitted between which kg_entity types; enforced by kg_ontology constraints
Navigating the knowledge_graph along kg_relationship edges to discover connected kg_entities; the fundamental operation enabling associative retrieval
The atomic unit of a knowledge_graph: a (subject kg_entity, predicate label, object kg_entity) tuple; equivalently a single kg_relationship with its endpoints
A structured repository of facts, rules, and assertions; unlike embedding-based retrieval, supports symbolic reasoning and logical inference
Temporal boundary in model's parametric knowledge; events after this date must be retrieved from external sources for accurate responses.
A graph-structured representation of entities and their relationships; used as a structured form of semantic_memory with traversable edges
Fetching factual or conceptual information from a knowledge source to ground LLM responses in verified information rather than parametric memory
The infrastructure and format for persisting knowledge — graph databases, triple stores, or vector databases — that supports knowledge_retrieval
The key-value tensors cached during transformer self-attention to avoid recomputing activations for previously-seen tokens
Applying compression (pruning, quantization) to kv_cache to fit more context within GPU memory
Strategies for storing, evicting, or compressing key-value tensors; critical for long contexts where cache size can exceed model size.
Strategies — including paged_attention, quantization, and eviction — to reduce the memory footprint of key_value_caching
Total key-value tensor dimensions constrained by context_length; scales as layers times heads times kv_dim times context_length
Attention approximated with linear complexity O(n) by kernelizing the attention operation; trades expressiveness for efficiency. Examples: Linformer, Performer, RFA.
Hashing scheme preserving similarity relationships; used in approximate_nearest_neighbor for fast vector_database queries
Working with context_window sizes significantly beyond standard (e.g., >32k tokens); presents engineering and quality challenges
Information persisted across sessions, tasks, or deployments; requires external storage and retrieval mechanisms since it cannot fit in context_window
The empirical finding that LLMs struggle to retrieve information placed in the middle of a long context, even when both ends are accessible
Selective State Space Model with input-dependent transition matrices; achieves transformer-quality at linear complexity, strong on long sequences.
The absolute token ceiling of the model architecture; synonymous with context_length when no additional constraints apply.
The parameter specifying the maximum number of tokens the model may output; also used colloquially as the token budget for any portion of context
The highest valid integer position index representable by the position_embedding scheme within context_length; equal to max_model_tokens minus one for zero-indexed sequences.
Pattern of reads/writes to memory over time; affects caching efficiency, prefetching strategies, and storage layout optimization.
Mechanism for locating specific information in memory; includes content-based and location-based addressing modes
Time since memory entry was written; used in recency-based eviction and for user awareness of information freshness.
Fraction of context_length reserved for working_memory versus content tokens; memory_efficiency depends on minimizing this fraction
High-importance tokens serving as retrieval keys or summarization seeds; stable points for memory reconstruction
Adding new information to an existing memory entry without modifying prior content; common for conversation logs and evolving facts
Systematic review of stored memories for accuracy, relevance, and compliance; governance practice for long_term_memory systems
LLM architecture with explicit external memory read/write gates; the model learns to access memory rather than relying solely on parameters.
Architecture combining neural computation with external memory storage; hybrid approach to memory_hierarchy management
Rate at which memory can be read/written; bounded by context length (read), storage system latency (external), and compute for embedding generation.
Associating related memories together (entity with attributes, event with participants); enables coherent retrieval of related facts
Maximum storable items in a memory system; bounded by context_length for working_memory and storage size for long_term_memory
Periodic save of memory state enabling recovery; critical for long-running agents or systems where interruption is possible.
The property that memory entries are consistent with each other and free of contradictions
Reducing memory footprint through summarization, extraction, or learned encoding; trades context_fidelity for capacity
Generation of plausible but incorrect memories when episodic_memory retrieval fails or produces false matches
Situations where multiple memory entries contain contradictory information; requires resolution strategies to maintain memory_coherence
Ensuring that reads from memory always reflect the most recent writes; critical in multi-agent or concurrent memory access scenarios
Verifying memory state is coherent: no contradictions, proper versioning, no orphaned references. Important for complex multi-source memory.
The process of transforming short-term memory representations into longer-term storage; converting ephemeral state to persistent records
Gradual degradation or lowering of retrieval priority for older memory entries over time, mimicking biological forgetting curves
Mathematical model of how memory strength decreases over time without reinforcement; governs episodic_memory eviction timing
Removing a specific memory entry from storage; used for privacy compliance, error correction, or memory_gc
Ratio of useful information retained per unit of memory storage or context_token budget
Attention implementation variants (flash_attention, sparse_attention) that reduce memory complexity from O(n²) to near-linear
The process of converting information into form suitable for storage; in vector stores, embedding generation; in model context, attention-based encoding.
Encrypting stored memories to protect sensitive information; affects retrieval latency due to decryption overhead.
The policy-driven removal of entries from memory when storage limits are reached, analogous to cache eviction strategies
Deliberate or algorithmic removal of memory entries deemed irrelevant, outdated, or harmful to preserve storage efficiency and signal quality
Memory spread across storage in ways that hurt retrieval efficiency; defragmentation or reorganization improves performance.
Garbage collection of memory entries — removing stale, contradicted, or superseded entries to maintain a clean, accurate memory store

The layered structure of LLM memory: immediate context (working), retrieved context (RAG), fine-tuned weights (parametric), external stores (vector DB). Each layer has different latency/capacity tradeoffs.
Computed or learned value of a memory item; determines retention priority in importance_weighted_memory systems
Scoring memories by significance so high-importance entries are retained, retrieved more frequently, or given priority in context_selection
New memories disrupting or overwriting related old memories; challenge for continual learning in episodic_memory systems
Removing or updating outdated memories; necessary when world_model facts change and stored memories become incorrect
Direct access to specific memory entries by identifier rather than content similarity; faster but requires knowing what you're looking for.
Combining information from multiple memory entries into a unified representation, resolving overlaps and conflicts
Condition where accumulated memory exceeds storage capacity; triggers eviction or compression strategies
Replacing a memory entry entirely with new content, used when prior information is superseded or fundamentally incorrect
How long memory survives; session memory (within conversation), user memory (across sessions), or permanent memory (until explicitly deleted).
Corruption of long_term_memory stores with false or harmful content; defense requires verification and source attribution
Aggregating multiple similar memories into a single representative memory; reduces storage while preserving key information
Situation where memory demand exceeds capacity; triggers eviction, compression, or retrieval of summarized memories.
Retrieving relevant information from stored memory; in external memory systems, this is vector search; in working context, this is attention-based retrieval.
Time to retrieve relevant memory entries; determined by embedding model, vector index size, and search algorithm. Critical for real-time applications.
Re-encoding or updating memory entries to maintain relevance or accuracy; more sophisticated than simple overwrite.
Re-presenting past experiences or interactions to the LLM during training or reasoning to reinforce memory consolidation and prevent catastrophic forgetting
The process of adjudicating memory_conflicts by choosing which entry takes precedence or synthesizing a consensus view
Measure of how long information remains accessible in memory systems; affected by eviction policies, storage capacity, and retrieval interference.
The act of fetching stored memory entries — by semantic similarity, keyword, metadata, or temporal proximity — to include in context
The query representation used to access memory; typically embedding of current context or explicit query, matched against stored keys.
What entities a memory applies to: user-specific, session-specific, global, or task-specific. Different scopes have different persistence requirements.
Querying memory stores using semantic similarity, exact match, or structured filters to surface relevant prior information
Dedicated positions in context reserved for memory operations; model learns to read/write at specific slots analogous to working memory buffers.
Maximum information storable in a memory system; bounded by vector store size, database rows, or context window tokens.
Compressing memory entries into shorter representations; can be extractive (selecting key sentences) or abstractive (LLM-generated summaries).
Record of memory accesses over time; useful for auditing, optimization, and understanding retrieval patterns. May be explicit or derived from query logs.
Modifying existing memory entries to reflect new information, corrections, or changed circumstances
Tracking changes to memory over time; enables rollback, audit, and understanding of how knowledge evolves.
The subset of episodic_memory available for retrieval at any time; analogous to context_window but for long_term_storage
Subset of memory_window extractable at any moment; constrained by current context_length utilization
Storing new information into memory after or during LLM inference; may include structuring, tagging, or deduplication of the incoming data
Extremely long context_window designs targeting one million or more tokens; requires architectural breakthroughs to be tractable
The architecture-specified maximum sequence length baked into model weights; represents the positional_embedding range and attention matrix dimensions
Running multiple self_attention operations in parallel with different learned projections; enables attending to different representation subspaces
Architecture with differentiable memory read/write operations; foundational concept for memory_augmented_network designs
Skills and procedures not consciously recalled; maps to procedural_memory encoded in model weights
NTK-aware RoPE scaling that treats frequency bands differently; preserves resolution on high-frequency components while interpolating low-frequency for long contexts.
Portion of token_budget reserved for model-generated response tokens; computed as token_budget minus input_capacity minus scratchpad_reservation
The portion of token_budget reserved for generated tokens; determined by max_tokens parameter or model ceiling minus input
The portion of context_length reserved for generated tokens; equals context_length minus input_token_budget minus overhead tokens.
The position or token count at which the model behavior shifts from normal processing to truncation or error; often slightly below context_boundary.
Chunking strategy where adjacent chunks share boundary tokens to prevent information loss at chunk_boundaries
A kv_cache management technique borrowed from OS page tables that enables efficient memory utilization across variable-length contexts
Knowledge encoded in model weights; requires no external retrieval but cannot be updated without fine-tuning. Changes slowly through continual learning.
Memory that survives across API calls and sessions; stored in a database, file, or key-value store and explicitly injected into context at inference time
Memory stored on disk or distributed database; enables scale beyond RAM but adds retrieval latency. Common for long-term agent memory.
Stable traits and preferences of a character or agent persona; maintained across sessions via system_message or retrieved context
Memory capturing user preferences, communication style, and facts about user; accumulated over multiple interactions for personalized responses.
Encoding that injects positional information into token representations since attention is permutation-invariant. Choices: sinusoidal, RoPE, ALiBi. Affects how context scales.
Ordinal integer from zero to context_window_boundary representing each token's location in the sequence; each index must be encodable by the position_embedding scheme in use
Technique extending context_window by interpolating position embeddings between known ranges; avoids extrapolation failures
Learned user preferences accumulated over interactions; used to personalize responses without explicit instruction each turn
Caching the KV tensors for shared prefixes (system prompt, few-shot examples) so they aren't recomputed per request; reduces latency and compute for repeated contexts.
Fraction of context_length saved from recomputation when shared prefixes exist; improves memory_efficiency for repeated system prompts
Learning a small continuous prefix that modifies model behavior; prefix is prepended to all layers, effectively conditioning without explicit context tokens.
Better recall of tokens at the start of context; often exploited by placing critical information at context boundaries.
Memory encoding how to perform tasks — skill sequences, workflows, or learned procedures — enabling agents to execute without re-instruction
Iterative refinement of notes expanding key points; applied to memory_consolidation where summaries become summaries-of-summaries
The actual user-available input tokens after subtracting context_overhead from input_capacity
Crafting input text to elicit desired outputs; includes instruction design, example selection, formatting, and context structuring.
Malicious content in retrieved context designed to override system instructions; mitigated by content filtering, separation markers, or retrieval source validation.
Parameterized structure for prompts; variables substituted per request. Critical for consistent context injection across many calls.
Semantic similarity between retrieval query and context entries; determines whether retrieved content helps answer the query.
Breaking complex question into simpler sub-questions answered separately then synthesized; handles multi-hop questions without requiring long context.
Expanding a short query into multiple related queries to increase recall; techniques: synonym expansion, HyDE hypotheses, sub-query decomposition.
Transforming user queries to improve retrieval from vector_database; includes expansion, reformulation, and decomposition
Tendency for models to weight recent tokens more heavily; may cause older context to be underutilized regardless of relevance.
Better recall of tokens at the end of context; often exploited by placing answers or key info near the end.
Encoding the relative distance between tokens rather than absolute positions; improves generalization to unseen context_lengths
Computing importance of retrieved candidates for current query; determines which long_term_memory enters working_memory
Storage of past experiences for retrieval; in fine-tuning, selected to reinforce important or rare patterns
Scoring retrieved candidates with a cross-encoder for finer relevance; expensive but more accurate than embedding similarity. Used as final step in retrieval pipelines.
Architecture pattern where an LLM queries external knowledge sources and injects results into context before generating a response; combines memory_retrieval with generation
Adjusting retrieval thresholds based on confidence estimates to balance recall and precision in long_term_memory access
When no relevant results are returned from memory; handled by query reformulation, relaxing constraints, or fallback to parametric knowledge.
Combining results from multiple retrieval strategies (semantic, keyword, graph) into a unified context set
Time required to fetch relevant items from long_term_memory into working_memory; affects real-time responsiveness
Fraction of retrieved chunks that are relevant to the query; high precision means fewer irrelevant tokens polluting context.
Fraction of all relevant information that was retrieved; low recall means the model misses critical facts. Tradeoff with context length limits.
Alignment between retrieved memory content and current generation needs; measured by relevance_scoring mechanisms
Tokens in context representing retrieved information; either as raw text chunks or as special [RETRIEVE] tokens triggering retrieval at generation time.
Distributed sliding_window_attention across multiple devices with communication-avoiding algorithms for very long sequences
context_length divided by number of devices in ring_attention; each device handles this many contiguous positions
A sliding_context_window variant maintaining a fixed-size suffix of conversation_history as the primary context for each new turn
Rotary Position Embedding encodes position via rotation in feature space; enables better generalization to longer contexts than absolute positions.
Modifying Rotary Position Embeddings to handle contexts longer than training: either linear interpolation (dims scaled) or NTK-aware scaling that preserves high-frequency details.
A position encoding method rotating the key and query vectors; enables extrapolation beyond the training context_length
Explicit intermediate reasoning space written by the model itself; a form of ephemeral working_memory externalized to tokens
Identifying and retaining only the most relevant tokens from a context; reduces context_length while preserving signal
The mechanism by which transformer models relate each token position to all other positions; the quadratic bottleneck in context_length scaling
Sampling multiple reasoning paths and selecting most common final answer; improves reliability on reasoning tasks by exploiting model uncertainty.
Self-Retrieval-Augmented Generation: model generates special tokens indicating whether to retrieve, if retrieved content is relevant, and whether to use it.
Memory storing general world knowledge, facts, and concepts rather than specific personal experiences; queried via retrieval for grounding
Graph of concepts connected by typed edges; models can store and traverse this structure for relational reasoning
Search over a corpus using meaning rather than keyword overlap; maps queries and documents to a shared embedding space for similarity comparison
Measure of meaning overlap between two text fragments in embedding_space; the basis for associative_memory retrieval
Embedding an entire sentence or paragraph as a single vector; the granularity most commonly used in semantic_search
A language-independent subword_tokenization framework that trains directly on raw text without pre-tokenization; used by many LLMs
The maximum contiguous token span a single forward pass can process; equals context_ceiling for standard models but differs for sliding_window architectures
The ordinal index of a token within the full context sequence; constrained to be less than or equal to maximum_position.
Information scoped to the current user interaction session; reset between sessions unlike persistent long_term_memory
Memory scoped to a single user session; includes conversation_history and ephemeral state accumulated during that session
Information retained within a single conversation session; typically implemented as rolling conversation_history limited by context_window
The general problem of finding items in a collection most similar to a query item; the operational form of vector_search
A context_management strategy where the active window slides forward, discarding the oldest tokens as new ones are added
Fixed-size contiguous subset of recent tokens kept in working_memory as new tokens arrive and old ones are evicted
A sparse_attention variant attending only to a local window of neighboring tokens; efficient for processing long sequences
Token distance from current position at which sliding_window begins evicting old tokens; bounded by context_length
Attention producing weighted averages over all positions; differentiable but computationally expensive at scale
Learned continuous embeddings prepended to context instead of discrete tokens; enables task-specific adaptation without fine-tuning full model.
Attention patterns that compute fewer than n² pairwise interactions, reducing memory_efficient_attention cost at the cost of expressiveness
A high-dimensional vector with mostly zero values; used in sparse_retrieval to represent documents as weighted term vectors
Retrieval using sparse representations like BM25 or TF-IDF; efficient for exact or lexical matches but limited for semantic queries
Environmental or positional information attached to memories enabling location-based retrieval
Sequence model (Mamba, S4) operating as continuous-time recurrence; offers linear scaling with sequence length and selective state propagation.
Monitoring entities and their properties over a conversation; a core capability requiring working_memory or explicit context
Processing context incrementally as it arrives rather than waiting for complete context; enables handling of very long or infinite streams.
A constituent question from a decomposed query; answered independently then combined. Each sub-question has simpler retrieval needs.
Tokenization breaking words into subword units (bytes, characters, morphemes) enabling open-vocabulary encoding with bounded vocabulary size
Compressing text by extracting or abstracting key content; used for memory_consolidation and context_overflow management
Persistent preamble injected into every conversation turn; anchors persona, behavioral rules, and long_term_memory instructions
Static instruction injected at conversation start defining model behavior; often contains role, constraints, output format. Loaded into context once per session.
Memory specific to a current task or goal; created at task start, used during task, discarded at completion.
Associating memories with timestamps enabling recency-based retrieval and temporal reasoning
Arranging memories by time of occurrence; supports recency-based retrieval and chronological reasoning
The process of transforming raw text into a dense vector representation in a learned high-dimensional space
Architecture separating working_memory, episodic_memory, and long_term_memory with different retrieval latencies and capacities
OpenAI's fast BPE tokenizer implementation in Rust; the standard tokenization backend for GPT-series models
Tracking token usage across context_building operations to ensure neither context_window nor max_tokens limits are exceeded
The positional delimiter marking the transition from input context to output generation; tokens before this marker are provided context, tokens after are to be generated.
The total token allocation available for a given context operation, encompassing both input context and output generation capacity
The ratio of semantic content units per token for a given text under a particular tokenization_scheme; affects how much text fits within context_length.
Maximizing the information density per token in context — eliminating redundancy and noise to extract more useful content per token spent
The arithmetic difference between current position or token count and context_boundary; the remaining room before overflow_threshold is reached.
Strategies to reduce token consumption without degrading downstream task performance — compression, selection, and smarter chunking
Converting raw text into tokens consumable by an LLM tokenizer; the foundational step before any context_building or memory operation
Varying token counts for same text across tokenizers; different models (cl100k vs tiktoken vs sentencepiece) have different tokenization schemes.
The specific algorithm determining how raw text is segmented into discrete tokens; determines token_boundary_marker positions and token_density for any given text.
Identifying the subject matter of conversation segments; enables routing to appropriate long_term_memory
Explicitly exploring multiple reasoning branches as a tree; more thorough than single chain-of-thought but requires more context tokens.
A specialized database for RDF-style knowledge representations: subject-predicate-object triples enabling SPARQL queries over knowledge_graph
Token position index where context_overflow becomes imminent and truncation_strategy must execute; typically context_length minus N reserved tokens
Policy for removing old context when context_overflow occurs; options include FIFO, importance-weighted, and semantic summarization
Personalized memory about a specific user maintained across sessions; enables continuity and personalization.
Memory tracking a specific user's demonstrated preferences, communication style, and requirements for personalized responses
Storage system indexing embeddings for similarity search; backbone of RAG. Examples: Pinecone, Weaviate, Chroma, FAISS. Enables retrieval from vast document collections.
Performing nearest-neighbor search in a high-dimensional embedding space; the core retrieval mechanism behind semantic_search
A subword_tokenization algorithm using greedy longest-match-first splitting; used by BERT and many encoder models
The transient token budget allocated for active reasoning within a single model call; scratch space for chain_of_thought and intermediate results
Internal representation of environment state enabling planning and reasoning; built from episodic_memory and semantic_memory
Model performs unseen task without examples; relies on instruction-following capabilities and knowledge from pretraining.
